title: What 20 seconds of sunlight did to her retina ☀️
subject: eye
description:
Have you ever glanced at the Sun during an eclipse? 👇

Can looking at the Sun damage your eyes? In 2017, a 26-year-old in New York watched the eclipse through the wrong glasses, and doctors at Mount Sinai later imaged a crescent-shaped burn on her retina. Solar retinopathy is painless, which is why people don't notice it happening.

Sources: Mount Sinai Health System press release (Dec 7, 2017); JAMA Ophthalmology case report by Mount Sinai ophthalmologists incl. Avnish Deobhakta (2017); The Washington Post ("The solar eclipse burned a crescent wound on a woman's retina", Dec 8, 2017); Live Science (solar eclipse eye damage)

can the sun burn your eyes

scenes.text: You can burn your retina without feeling a thing.
On August 21, 2017, 26-year-old Nia Payne stepped outside on Staten Island for the eclipse.
She looked up for about 6 seconds, then 15 to 20 more through borrowed glasses that weren't real eclipse glasses.
Nothing hurt. The retina doesn't feel pain.
Then a dark crescent sat in the middle of her vision, shaped like the eclipse.
At Mount Sinai, doctors found that crescent burned into her photoreceptors. There's no treatment.
